newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Western Sahara talks end a day early.
newsitem.headline: Western Sahara talks end a day early.

text.p: High-level direct talks between Morocco and its Western Sahara foes, the Polisario Front, ended a day ahead of schedule in Lisbon on Tuesday, Portuguese diplomatic sources said.

The two sides, who fought a 16-year bush war over the vast, mineral-rich territory, met for the first time on Monday in the presence of United Nations mediators, led by former U.S. secretary of state James Baker.
Baker was due to give a news conference at 1800 GMT.
The sources declined to say why the talks had ended ahead of schedule, but one official said the mood of the delegations was sad.
"The delegations are going home to consult with their respective leaders," one source said.

The United Nations successfully brokered a ceasefire in 1991 but has since failed to implement a proposed referendum on the future of the 250,000 square km (100,000 sq mile) territory because Morocco and the Algeria-backed Polisario cannot agree on who should be allowed to vote.
